subject: HyperTools — Post-call: SDK integration, function-calls & next steps
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Emily Zhang <emily.zhang@hypertools.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jul 2025 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: HyperTools — Post-call: SDK integration, function-calls & next steps

Hi Emily — thanks again for the time on the call just now. Quick recap of what we heard and proposed next steps so we stay aligned. Please flag anything I missed or got wrong.

Key pain points you shared:
- Search relevancy drops when users move from short queries to multi-sentence prompts (context/embeddings drift).
- Current latency on batch reranking is ~600-900ms which affects UX for list refreshes.
- Engineering bandwidth constraints: your infra team prefers minimal SDK changes and a single integration point.

Goals you want to hit:
- Sub-300ms median cold-start rerank latency for top-10 candidates
- Keep CPU footprint low on application servers (push inference work to Redwood)
- Maintain ability to call structured outputs and function-calling from the same pipeline

Product/Integration recap (what we suggested)
- SDK change: light-touch client update. We propose using Redwood’s streaming generator SDK to do: prefix caching + streaming tokens to UI while a background rerank completes. Minimal client surface: initialize client, call streamGenerate + call embeddings/rerank endpoint.
- Function calling: use our structured-output mode to map model outputs to your internal action schema (we showed example mapping).
- Embeddings/reranking: store candidate embeddings in your vector DB; call Redwood’s reranker endpoint to score and return deterministic ranks. We suggested an L2-normalized dense embedding with an OpenSearch vector store (your team already uses it).

Immediate next steps (agreed):
1) Redwood to deliver a short integration proposal and sample SDK patch (2 business days) — includes sample function-calling schema and streaming snippet.
2) HyperTools to provide a small dataset of 250 representative queries + candidate lists for a benchmark test (target by end of week).
3) Schedule a technical session w/ Marcus (solutions engineering) to walk through the sample integration and perf tuning (30–45m) — propose Thu 7/17 or Fri 7/18.

Attachments: I will attach a compact proposal and a mapping CSV that shows the field-level mapping we recommended (ETAs below).

If this looks right I’ll circulate the proposal and lock in Marcus’ session.

Thanks — talk soon.

—
Rachel Kim

Hi Emily — quick technical follow-up ahead of Thu’s session. Attaching two small artifacts and a short checklist.

Summarized approach (TL;DR):
1) Client flow (Node + Python): call stream_generate() to present an interim answer; concurrently call reranker.rerank_batch() using candidate embeddings fetched from your OpenSearch. When rerank completes, swap results atomically on the client UI. We include an "update_token" idempotency header so the client can ignore late responses for stale requests.

2) Deterministic UX options:
- Option A (recommended): stream a concise summary (max 60 tokens) + show "ranking in progress" spinner. Replace list when reranker returns. This avoids content flicker and preserves immediacy.
- Option B: block on rerank for interactive flows (adds ~150–300ms depending on batch size).

3) Perf knobs I’ll bring to the call:
- Batch size: start 16 candidates; tune up to 64 for throughput.
- KV cache: 1h TTL for session-affine prompts; store prefix cache on Redwood to reduce cold-starts.
- Quantization: try int8 per-tensor for the reranker model; expect 1.4–1.8x perf improvement with minor quality loss.

Attachments (stubs):
- node_python_snippets.txt (code snippets for stream + rerank)
- perf_baseline_table.csv (sample numbers from similar customers)

Links I’ll bring in the session:

- HubSpot deal: https://hubspot.example/deal/HT-2025-078

See you Thu 7/17 10:00 PT. I will also include a short demo that shows the atomic swap behavior.
